metadata.collection_notes: Data extracted from the hardcoded var REVIEWS array in dreamcast.html and moved to outputs/gamespot_dreamcast_reviews.json. Page now fetches from this file.

review.blurb: Think state of the art.
With NFL 2K's incredible control, you feel as though you're down on the field with the NFL's finest.
In the end, NFL 2K1 is a deeper, more refined version of the original game.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 is a must-own Dreamcast game.
The improvements in the game, although subtle on the surface, are substantial for serious fans of the NBA.
Visual Concepts has tweaked and buffed out the annoying gameplay traits that plagued its original hoops game, and the result is a highly polished product.
If you're a racing game fan, you really owe it to yourself to give Le Mans a try.
Fans of the NFL 2K series will undoubtedly find that it's hard not to like NFL 2K2.
To call it a must-own game is a definite understatement.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater is a classic in every sense of the word, and the Dreamcast port is the version that is best suited to stand the tests of time.
Quake III Arena for the Dreamcast marks one of the few times that a PC first-person shooter has moved over to a console system without sacrificing much of its playability or options.
Rayman 2 is one of the best platforming experiences available today.
Quake III Arena on the Dreamcast may offer more visceral gameplay, but Unreal Tournament is the most complete package yet.
Skies of Arcadia is the product of a legacy of role-playing games that hearkens back to Sega's earliest days in the home console market.
With the Chao-breeding simulation and the minigames, Sonic offers much more beyond the completion of its story.
Overall, UFC successfully merges the ease of play you'd expect from a fighting game with the simulation aspects of a sports game.
Dead or Alive 2 is the hardest-hitting game in town.

F355 Challenge is the best driving game currently available on any console, let alone the Dreamcast, and once you crest the game's steep learning curve, the addictive need to constantly best other players' lap times will provide weeks of replayability.
Jet Grind Radio is one of those "something for everyone" games that really make a perfect addition to the Dreamcast library.
Soul Reaver is a deep game possessed of myriad impressive little touches.
While I wouldn't call Marvel vs. Capcom the most balanced fighting game in the world, it makes up for its shortcomings by simply being a whole lot of fun.
NFL Blitz 2001 for Dreamcast is a worthy update and a giant step above the PlayStation and Nintendo 64 versions of the same name.
Samba De Amigo is one of the best music and rhythm games released thus far, and it's the first such game to hit the United States, making it an excellent entry into the world of music peripherals.

The Dreamcast version of Alpha 3 keeps all the great modes and additions from the PlayStation version but also uses the more powerful hardware to its benefit, delivering larger character sizes, sharper and more colorful graphics, and extremely minimal load times.
It's an inviting, fast-paced, technical rally game that offers enough replay value and features to satiate any racing audience.
NBA 2K almost does for basketball what NFL 2K did for football.
Sega Rally 2 marries the qualities of super-fun arcade racing, challenging track elements and design, grease-monkey tinkering, and unparalleled replay value.
The game has the same kind of universal appeal and pick-up-and-play mentality that made Tony Hawk's Pro Skater a hit on the PlayStation. As such, it's a must-buy for any Dreamcast owner.
Pass interference is no longer a penalty - it's a necessity.
It's definitely a worthy and much-needed update to a long-running series.
Ready 2 Rumble is one of the must-have launch games on the Dreamcast.
IMPORT: It's a polished game that serves as a showcase for the DC and the evolution of the RPG genre, and fans should definitely find a way to play it.
The concept sounds extremely strange, but in practice, Typing of the Dead is extremely fun.
While it would have been nice to see some slightly more drastic changes to the Crazy Taxi formula, fans of the original will immediately feel right at home with Crazy Taxi 2.
A greater variety of tracks, cars, and options makes this sequel seem fresh and new, while the addition of Internet play provides an assurance that you'll enjoy the game for many months to come.
Who would have thought that the publisher responsible for some of the slowest games on the planet would come up with a game that leaves its own classic mech series in the dust?
If you own a Dreamcast, and you're reading this to find out if NHL 2K is worth your hard-earned dollars, the answer is yes.
Sega Bass Fishing 2 is a model example of what sequels should be.
Sonic Adventure 2 is an addictive platform game, whose gifts beckon you to come back and enjoy its entertaining and fast-paced gameplay system.
A game that carries the level of polish, playability, and fun that Tech Romancer does deserves to see a handful of sequels, each building on the mythos established here.

games.title: The King of Fighters Dream Match 1999
games.index_title: The King of Fighters Dream Match 1999

review.blurb: A definite must for 2D fighting-game fans.
Dreamcast owners craving a genuinely compelling gameplay experience would do well to check out Bangai-O.

games.title: Fatal Fury: Mark of the Wolves
games.index_title: Fatal Fury: Mark of the Wolves

review.blurb: It's a port of one of SNK's last great NeoGeo games. It's also one of the last great games for the Dreamcast.
Fans of space shooters owe themselves the opportunity to play Ikaruga, a game that was designed both to impress their sensibilities and to challenge every ounce of their being.
The game capably competes against any other college football product on the market.
Tennis 2K2 honors the look and feel of the original Virtua Tennis, but the innovations made may not be enough to warrant a purchase for those veteran Virtua Tennis players out there.
Fans of the off-kilter action found in the previous versus games will surely be pleased with Marvel vs. Capcom 2, as it represents the first major set of changes the series has ever seen.
Like the other Worms games, World Party appears simplistic at first, but it actually packs a level of deep strategic value that other games in the genre could only hope to achieve.
Aerowings 2 boils down to excellent gameplay, copious replay, and creamy visuals, marred ever so slightly by chintzy music.
Jojo's Bizarre Adventure offers fine-tuned Capcom quality with a twist, along with a unique storyline and great control.
Despite its few flaws, MDK 2 is a great first effort by BioWare, and it's a better game than the original.
Resident Evil 3 Nemesis remains a very worthwhile game even though not much has been added to the translation.
Issues of balance aside, Capcom has produced a great game.
In short, Sonic Team has created a party experience for the ages - like Bomberman, the best idea is to grab a bunch of friends and go head-to-head.
It's the kind of game that titles like Eidos' Deathtrap Dungeon and Universal's Xena: Warrior Princess should have been.

games.title: Ecco the Dolphin: Defender of the Future
games.index_title: Ecco the Dolphin: Defender of the Future

review.blurb: Ecco holds up the standards of creative execution that Sega has set for its flagship titles and simultaneously makes clearer the potential for artistry in video games.
Even with its shallow storyline and camera issues, Phantasy Star Online simply manages to be a whole lot of fun.
Speed Devils is an arcade-style racing game along the general lines of Midway's Crusin' series and California Speed... except it doesn't suck.
For Joe Blow on the street, Soul Calibur is still the better choice, but Virtua Fighter fans will find all they need neatly wrapped in this package.
While it's not the Dreamcast's best racer, 4x4 Evolution offers an adequate challenge, rewarding gameplay, and the ability to build your own truck and take it online for some action.

If you invest in one or two dancemats along with the game, Dance Dance Revolution is an amazingly fun game that you can play alone or in large groups, provided no one is too embarrassed to get busy in front of a crowd.
While Deep Fighter isn't destined for any awards, the game's intriguing storyline, solid gameplay, and sharp graphics make playing it a pleasurable experience.
All things considered, The Last Blade 2 for the Dreamcast is a faithful port of a good game.
NHL 2K2 is a great game of hockey that any hockey fan who owns a Dreamcast should really consider picking up.
As long as you're not expecting Quake III Arena and are ready for a steep learning curve, Rainbow Six is as deep and challenging as action games get.
Roommania #203 is a well-made game, especially in the storytelling and sound departments.
Vanishing Point is an excellent racing game marred by the developer's attempts to overcomplicate things.
Tennis fans should be in heaven after playing Virtua Tennis.
In the end, Virtual On: Oratorio Tangram is one of the most visually impressive Dreamcast games yet, alongside Soul Calibur and Shenmue.
With its better balance, new features, and addictive gameplay, PSO Version 2 stands out as one of the last great games for the system.
As a four-player game, it's definitely one of the wildest fighters to come to the Dreamcast.
IMPORT: It's definitely unique and uniquely Sega, and the Dreamcast game library needs more wacky games like this - Seaman needs the company.
Seldom missing a beat when compared with its cabinet-bound counterpart, Rush 2049 is the ideal home port of an arcade game.
IMPORT: It's cut from the same cloth as countless other Capcom fighting games, but it's got more features, more characters, and more depth than a lot of them.
Game Arts has put together a solid RPG with Grandia II, even if it isn't as deep or difficult as the original.
The best boat-racing game to hit arcades has made its way to the Dreamcast - but what it hasn't done is brought anything new with it.
Maken X would make a great addition to an already strong library.
It's a great game to own, but this version is not an essential purchase.
While Armada isn't for everyone, it is unique, fun, and original.
It won't keep you entertained forever, but if you can get around its lack of length, Cannon Spike delivers.
Infogrames has lifted a formerly average game on the PlayStation to greatness on the Dreamcast.
International Track & Field is an excellent title.
While the game may not hold up in terms of long-lasting value, those looking for a quick fishing fix without getting dirty will be more than pleased with this offering.
Indeed, while Shenmue is revolutionary, the game is far from perfect.

games.title: Sword of the Berserk: Guts' Rage
games.index_title: Sword of the Berserk: Guts' Rage

review.blurb: Sword of the Berserk is the best Final Fight-type game to appear in ages.
With the exception of random AI, Wacky Races is a license-based racing game done right.
Worms Armageddon is designed so you can play with other people, and the single-player match is really no substitute.
Metropolis Street Racer is a beautiful racer with accurate physics and tight control, but the kudos system makes it far more challenging than it needs to be.
Ready 2 Rumble Round 2 is a solid arcade-style boxing game, and like most arcade games, it wears thin fairly quickly.

Combining the fantastic audio from the PlayStation edition, the four-player mode offered on the Nintendo 64, and the graphical advances you expect from the Dreamcast, this version of V8SO is clearly the best of the three.
If you're not a huge fan of the game's seven track and field events or lack human competition to play with, the game will be nothing more than a weekend fantasy.
Despite its frustratingly flawed gameplay, World Series Baseball 2K2 is the Dreamcast's best baseball game.
This tank-based action game offers up a solid dose of good old-fashioned gameplay wrapped up in slick graphics and an innovative use of technology.
Mat Hoffman is easily the best BMX game on the Dreamcast.
Expect to enjoy it immensely for the first week or two, but don't expect to find very much long-term fun.
If multiplayer is not a big factor for you, Rogue Spear's single-player game is certainly worth the price of admission.
IMPORT: While a little low on gameplay, Sakura Taisen's focus on story and presentation is handled expertly.
Tokyo Xtreme Racer 2 is a decent game, but it's all been done before.
If the game's release had been more timely and the frame rate problems minimized, it might have been a Spring blockbuster.
NBA Showtime is a fun game, but its longevity is directly linked to the number of friends you have who are interested in the game.
Originally designed for the Naomi hardware in arcades, the Dreamcast version looks virtually identical to its coin-op counterpart.
Solid gameplay, numerous options, and attention to detail make Railroad Tycoon II an excellent simulation.
While it doesn't come close to tapping the graphic and audio capabilities of the system, the gameplay is still very solid, and it fills the futuristic racing niche for the Dreamcast nicely.

games.title: Walt Disney World Quest: Magical Racing Tour
games.index_title: Walt Disney World Quest: Magical Racing Tour

review.blurb: While it may be a Mario Kart clone, Magical Racing Tour does put forth a unique effort in two categories: graphics and sound.
A worthwhile investment for any hard-core racing-sim fan.
Star Wars Demolition might seem like some half-baked attempt to cash in on the Star Wars license, though it's actually a competently executed game.
If you skipped out on Double Impact - or if you're fanatical about your SFIII - 3rd Strike is a good, refined 2D fighter that won't disappoint.
Admittedly, more multiplayer and career options would have been nice, but in a game focused directly at fun-seeking race fanatics, what's present is ample enough.
More of a fishing game than a fishing simulator, Get Bass is a cool, if temporary, way to spend your time. No messy worms either.
Sega GT attempts to capture some of Gran Turismo's formula for the Dreamcast, but it ultimately falls short due to poor control and an unintuitive interface.
The main problem affecting the Dreamcast port of Soldier of Fortune is the game's ridiculously long loading times.
Those who've played any game in the Darkstalkers series will feel right at home with Vampire Chronicles.
The Dreamcast has a few solid puzzle games, but Bust-A-Move 4 is neither a new breed nor a game that will push the power of your Dreamcast to impressive new levels.
While far from perfect, it is easily the best surfing game on the market, but more importantly, it's also a fun game.
Ooga Booga is a lighthearted and somewhat original game, but it's not quite as addictive as the games it most closely resembles.
It starts slow, but Slave Zero builds into a pretty strong shooter that's worth checking out for its guns, bosses, and multiplayer mode.
Fans of the long-running comic series and players in search of the ever-elusive novel game would do themselves a favor by checking out Spider-Man.
There is definitely a lot to Street Fighter III.
Tomb Raider Chronicles is a worthy enough "sequel" to the original and can deliver an adequate number of thrills, though nothing unique or surprising.
Dino Crisis fails to take advantage of the Dreamcast hardware, resulting in a game that is structurally sound but visually average by Dreamcast standards.
There is no real reason why RPG fans shouldn't go for this one; it's a genuinely satisfying experience, even if it is a bit textbook in execution and scope.
Despite a plethora of design and gameplay issues, it's hard not to enjoy the cute and varied experience contained within the game's 30 areas.
What will make or break this game for you is really the original and unintuitive gameplay.
The less than engaging storyline and the heavy focus on defensive missions holds the game back and keeps it from being as good as the classics that made the genre popular.
Golf fans with a DC hooked up to their television will surely have a good time with the game, even though it isn't quite as compelling as similar games appearing on other platforms.
If you're interested in pulling some Tom Cruise-like maneuvers without any Kelly McGillis-style subplot, Air Force Delta will satisfy.
IMPORT: Cool Cool Toon is a sure bet for import-savvy rhythm game fans, who would be denying themselves some saccharine-drenched fun if they passed this one up.
Expendable is a refreshing blast of arcade gaming that never seems to get old.
The multiplayer mode, called fluffmatch, is really where the game earns most of its points.
You'd be hard-pressed to find a more visually impressive shooter on the Dreamcast, and the game is highly playable to boot.
Looney Tunes Space Race massages the retinas quite well, but the cheap AI and random power-ups place an unwanted emphasis on luck instead of skill.
Iif you're a broadband-adapter owner looking for something new that supports your woefully neglected device, Outtrigger fits the bill nicely.

Space Channel 5 absolutely oozes with style from beginning to end, and even though a bit of the game's charm has been lost in the translation from Japanese to English, it's still an interesting, yet criminally simplistic game.
Those who are looking for another game to play online with the Dreamcast should consider picking up this one.
If you're in the mood for a game where each event is reasonably well designed and integrated into a greater, meatier whole, then Infogrames' Xtreme Sports should prove satisfying.

games.title: Alone in the Dark: The New Nightmare
games.index_title: Alone in the Dark: The New Nightmare

review.blurb: The budget price of this game is sure to please just about any gamer willing to take the plunge into this well-saturated genre.
Red Storm hasn't done anything wrong with Bang! Gunship Elite, but the elimination of the multiplayer features found in the PC version of the game limits its appeal.
Bomberman Online takes an old standard and makes it feel at least somewhat fresh again.

games.title: Capcom vs. SNK: Millennium Fight 2000 Pro
games.index_title: Capcom vs. SNK: Millennium Fight 2000 Pro

review.blurb: IMPORT - Though its gameplay isn't especially deep, Millennium Fight Pro is an enjoyable slugfest that'll let you play with teams of some of the most popular 2D fighting-game characters ever created.
Puzzle gamers looking for a quality weekend rental need look no further than Frogger 2.
Grand Theft Auto 2 for the Dreamcast combines the feature set from the PlayStation version with the graphical sheen of the PC version.
Wipeout fans would do well to give Mag Force Racing a shot, at least as an interim solution until Fusion hits.
It's really one of the more interesting shooters to see a home release in recent times, and there's really no telling when another will be released.
It ultimately does what few updated classics do well - it brings new concepts to a well-known game while keeping the fun and magic of the original game.
NBA Hoopz for the Dreamcast is the same old song and dance that Midway has been perpetuating for years now.
This is sim country, baby, and it ain't for everyone.
If you're into games like The Legend of Zelda, Beyond Oasis, Alundra, or the original Legacy of Kain, then consider picking this one up.
If you like Diablo, you'll like Lodoss. If not, steer clear.
With a few more months, this game could have probably turned out a lot better.
Younger children will be delighted to be at the controls, but seasoned gamers will want to look elsewhere for a more polished and challenging experience.
IMPORT: Thanks the grassroots presentation, a relatively creative style of narrative, and an affordable price, El Dorado Gate Chapter 1 is a promising title.
Consider it short-lived fun, at best.
Shadow Man for the Dreamcast is truly the only console version of the game that isn't a chore to play.
Just a gun that lines up with the sights doesn't seem too much to ask for.
Toy Commander is exactly what you would imagine it to be.
Like Pilotwings 64, Aero Wings has realistic physics, and offers an authentic flying experience.
A severe lack of technological upgrades and cookie-cutter character design make this a tough game to recommend.
Visual issues aside, though, Seaman is a good game, provided you don't burn yourself out on it.

Overall, this game warrants a solid score for its many attributes - decent artificial intelligence (especially the goalies), nice animation, entertaining play modes, and multiplayer. But unfortunately the automatic player-switching throws a wet blanket over the fun.
KoF Evolution is about as good a port of SNK's The King of Fighters '99 as anyone could ask for.
18 Wheeler would be easier to recommend as a budget title; with a price comparable to more lasting games, however, it's probably best left as a rental.
The Dreamcast version of Army Men Sarge's Heroes is an engaging, albeit dated entry into the 3D action combat genre.
If you're new to the scene or you enjoyed last year's ECW Hardcore Revenge, Anarchy Rulz should keep you occupied until the next installment.
Rippin' Riders does look and sound very nice but has major issues in the control department and feels incomplete.
If you're expecting SmackDown! with better graphics and more modes, you'll be disappointed by Royal Rumble's tightly focused gameplay.
Despite its few frustrating control issues, Neo is a surprisingly polished product.
This game falls directly into the perfect-for-a-rental category, and it ultimately proves that you need more than great graphics to make a great game.
While it may disappoint dyed-in-the-wool Resident Evil fans, Dreamcast newcomers looking for an adventure fix on their new machine should be pleased.
Carrier isn't an awful game, and it really does manage to grow on you after a while, but it definitely has problems.
Hidden and Dangerous for the Dreamcast does little to improve upon the same product presented for the PC.
Seasoned fans of the freestyle sports genre will whip through Razor Freestyle Scooter in an afternoon, no questions asked.
If you're the kind of person who loves challenging tank games or happens to have a few trigger-happy friends, the game takes on a life of its own.
Die-hard action-game players will find the game far too easy and much too tedious to be of any real value, but children and Dr. Seuss fans should be well satisfied.
Treasure Strike is a fun multiplayer game, but if you're a solo gamer, be warned that it's not too exciting.
Kenji Eno has created one of the most engaging stories of all time and given it support in every way possible, except the one that matters most: gameplay.
Dragonriders is hardly a terrible game, but it has its share of issues and won't appeal to a large group of gamers.

games.title: Gundam Side Story: Rise from the Ashes
games.index_title: Gundam Side Story: Rise from the Ashes

review.blurb: One has to wonder why we should give a crap about sub-Gundam machinery like the GM.
Sno-Cross Championship Racing was a valiant effort on the PlayStation, on the Dreamcast it falls far short of standards and expectations.
Despite its impressive graphics and excellent voice acting, the simplistic and monotonous nature of Stupid Invaders' gameplay manages to drag down an otherwise entertaining experience.

games.title: Super Street Fighter II X for Matching Service
games.index_title: Super Street Fighter II X for Matching Service

review.blurb: IMPORT: The game is definitely close to arcade-perfect, but when you consider the game's age and its place in the Street Fighter universe, the resulting product isn't terribly impressive.
Aimed mainly at the C.A.R.T. fan, other Dreamcast owners waiting for a great racer would be better advised to look into Sega Rally 2.
If you've beaten Dynamite Cop in arcades there's no real reason to buy the game.
The interesting level design, copious eye candy, and heavily touted online play are crippled by the games fumbled controls.
The game puts even less of an emphasis on combat than Resident Evil-style games; instead it focuses more on the process of identifying, and subsequently neutralizing, traps.
Iron Aces tries a little too hard to please the simulation and action crowd simultaneously.
The game, as a whole, is a little too simplistic to hold the interest of most players, eventually relegating Pen Pen TriIcelon to the "especially good for younger players" category.
While it's all in import-friendly English, the game's evolution concept is extremely abstract and all too central to the game to make it truly enjoyable, regardless of the language.
This one says "rental" all over it.
If it weren't for that silly earthquake thing, Wetrix+ could have been a great puzzle game.
Charge 'N Blast doesn't have any glaring flaws, but it also doesn't excel in any general category.
Nightmare Creatures 2 is a good idea fumbling over itself to be better.

games.title: Toy Story 2: Buzz Lightyear to the Rescue
games.index_title: Toy Story 2: Buzz Lightyear to the Rescue

review.blurb: Overall, Activision has done a decent, if uninspired, job of porting the game to yet another platform.
If a good 16-bit shooter is what you're looking for, you could do a lot better elsewhere.
Kita He ("to the north") is the first game in the uniquely Japanese genre of dating simulations to hit the Dreamcast.
As a game, Silver is well-intentioned but flawed. It draws on a variety of console role-playing's staple elements, but never to truly great effect.

games.title: Star Wars Episode 1: Jedi Power Battles
games.index_title: Star Wars Episode 1: Jedi Power Battles

review.blurb: Jedi Power Battles is a reasonably fun game if you're a fan of Star Wars or if you're into vegetating in front of a standard action game for a few minutes at a time (or especially if you're both).
The Tetris 4D experience is not worth rushing out to buy a Dreamcast for.
Evolution 2 leaves you with the feeling that its cast of charming characters deserves a more effective vehicle.
Does the fact that Sega has added exclusive home-only features mean that Zombie Revenge is much more than a gussied-up arcade port? Not exactly.
ECW and its fans deserve better than this cookie-cutter approach to game design.
As it stands, Mr. Driller is good enough to keep you interested for a week or so, but it lacks any long-term staying power.
Fans of the Spawn comic book may enjoy this game for the simple fact that it's the prettiest Spawn game yet, but all others should rent with prejudice.
Sydney 2000 is good enough to compete at the Olympic level as far as video games go - but it'll be hard-pressed to earn anything above a bronze medal.
This is not a must-have Dreamcast launch game.
While it's slightly better than its PlayStation brother, Centipede is still only average, at best.
The DC version of this graphically intensive platform adventure is sometimes fun but gets very old very quickly.

games.title: Midway's Greatest Arcade Hits Volume I
games.index_title: Midway's Greatest Arcade Hits Volume I

review.blurb: If you're into classic arcade games, and you haven't already picked up this exact collection for the PlayStation or PC, this isn't a bad way to go.
Coaster Works is by no means a bad roller coaster simulator, but it's not an outstanding one either.
If you already possess these games in another format, the Dreamcast version is completely unnecessary.
Many games try to test your skill, but Super Runabout works to exercise your sense of frustration.
Tomb Raider: The Last Revelation reeks of a heartless cash-in and the game, for lack of a better term, simply has no soul.
If Sega's previous arcade light-gun games still hold appeal for you, this game may be right up your alley.
Supercross 2000 squanders an opportunity to be something new, and instead gives us the same thing we've played plenty of times before.
Re-Volt on the Dreamcast is clearly the best version of the three home editions, but it still remains an evilly unforgiving game.
Spec Ops: Omega Squad for the Dreamcast continues the substandard tradition of the series, and it is perhaps more flawed than any previous Spec Ops title.
What we have on display is a criminal waste of resources.
While those who are fans of the film might find some redeeming quality in Chicken Run, most should definitely avoid it.
Floigan Brothers has a distinct look and a clever concept, but these are its only strengths, and they aren't enough to support the rest of the game's numerous flaws.
In the end, when you take all of Omikron's various parts and add them together, the game doesn't amount to much.
While Time Stalkers' story is passable enough, its contradictory dungeon, battle, and experience system undermines any hope you may have had of enjoying this game.
It'll definitely be in importers' bargain bins before too long.
If you're looking for something to play online, Maximum Pool does the job, albeit without any bells or whistles.
Mortal Kombat Gold is sure to test even the biggest fan's faith in the line.
Experienced and discerning gamers would do well to steer clear of Buzz Lightyear of Star Command, as the game is simplistic and light.
One can't use high expectations to explain away all of WSB 2K1's flaws.
What could have been a decent game is marred by lackluster execution.
July is a disturbingly bland choose-your-own-adventure book that just happened into a Dreamcast port.
While the game may sport a spiffy set of tech specs, Rainbow Cotton's core gameplay is so flawed that it leaves the overall experience unsalvageable.
Playing Soul Fighter is a chore, thanks to tedious gameplay and even worse control.

It's clear that NFL QB Club 2001 is trying to play catch up with Sega's NFL 2K series, and the way things stand, QB Club still has a lot of cleaning up to do before it can smell as rosy fresh as Sega's superior offerings.
Virtua Striker 2 is a classic example of good ideas gone horribly wrong.
The added training mode in the home version doesn't make up for the fact that you can master the game in less than a day.
Do yourself a favor and buy an art book instead.
It was sort of weak on the PlayStation. On the Dreamcast it's a primped-up clone of a sort-of-weak game.
Die-hard survival-horror fans might possibly get a quick fix from this game, but even that's questionable.
TNN Motorsports HardCore Heat lacks any real punch and comes off as one of the few throwaway titles available at launch.

games.title: Evil Dead: Hail to the King
games.index_title: Evil Dead: Hail to the King

review.blurb: It's hard to believe that the survival-horror genre can only be done right by Capcom (and perhaps Konami), but Hail to the King will do little to convince you otherwise.
Instead of fixing any of Psycho Circus' problems, or adding some Dreamcast-only levels, the programmers at Tremor have actually removed some key features of the PC version.
Every single one of the ports is incredibly poor, resulting in nothing but disappointment for anyone looking to replay any of these classic games.
The combination of the unbearable load times, the smattering of minigames, and the poor minigame design make Sonic Shuffle a boring diversion at best.
Gigawing began as a CPS2 arcade game, and the difficulty that stems from these arcade roots is apparent - this game is impossible.
Spend five minutes playing Conflict Zone and you''ll understand why it should have stayed on the computer.
It's hard to recommend Death Crimson OX to anyone but the truly desperate light-gun fanatic.

Regardless of whether the original Gauntlet game was compelling enough to warrant an arcade remake, the Dreamcast version of Gauntlet Legends is a subpar button-masher that's neither interesting nor nostalgic.
Totally unrealistic physics, generic track design, and a vehicle list devoid of anything but topless roadsters make this a game to be avoided by the casual arcade-racing fan.
The PC version of this package does a far better job of emulating these classic Atari hits.
NBA 2Night is an admirable first effort, but the game feels unfinished in almost every aspect, particularly on the court.
Surf Rocket Racers is what happens when a game developer takes a stock game formula and simply goes nowhere with it.
The game itself isn't terrible, but unless you are absolutely aching to exercise the online capabilities of your Dreamcast, there is really no reason to pick up this game.
The repeating questions, repeating speech, and dull minigames keep it from being a game you'd want to pop in whenever you need a simple party-style game.
Awkward level design and poor presentation make the 2000 release of Q*Bert a dull endeavor.
If it weren't for the terrible control scheme, horribly accurate AI, and confusing terrain, this game would still be overly simple.

While the PlayStation version managed to be a fairly inoffensive game, the Dreamcast version's graphical flaws manage to wreck anything the game has going for it, leaving behind an ugly, unplayable mess.
There's really nothing exciting about Fighting Force 2.
Heavy Metal is simply an uninteresting licensed 3D arena shooter that feels extremely rushed and won't impress anyone.
IMPORT: Sorcerian is bad. Any fond memories of the original games will quickly be cast aside when you play the Dreamcast incarnation.
Unless you're extremely into the spy game genre, you should avoid this game at all costs.
It's not as if the Godzilla license has ever really turned out a good game, but that doesn't excuse Godzilla Generations from being as terrible as it is.

games.title: MTV Sports: Skateboarding Featuring Andy McDonald
games.index_title: MTV Sports: Skateboarding Featuring Andy McDonald

review.blurb: MTV Sports: Skateboarding Featuring Andy Macdonald serves no other purpose than to act as an excellent example of how not to make a skateboarding game.

Even though the Dreamcast may possess considerably more processing power under the hood than the Nintendo 64 or PlayStation, nothing seems to be able to hide the fact that South Park Rally is simply not a good game.
While the selection of gambling titles on the Dreamcast is slim in comparison to the PlayStation or the PC, the best bet for all involved would be to take your chips elsewhere.
Quarterback Club 2000 is a buggy, problem-ridden football game that should be avoided by all football video game fans.
Somewhere inside the Dreamcast version of Urban Chaos is a decent game, struggling to escape. But the layers and layers of flaws completely negate any strong points the game could have had.
You can pick up Puyo Puyo Da! and be completely fed up with it within an hour.

One could go on for hours ripping this game apart, harping on its intolerable load times, useless physics engine, or haphazard AI, but it all boils down to one inescapable fact: Spirit of Speed 1937 is abysmal.
Stay far, far away from this game.
